# COUNT ignores NULL arrays, not empty arrays or arrays with NULL elements.
# Source: third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/aggregate_functions.md.

# BigQuery's answer to unverified/function_types.txt: COUNT takes arrays of INTERVAL values.
SELECT COUNT(a) FROM UNNEST([STRUCT([INTERVAL 1 DAY] AS a), STRUCT(CAST(NULL AS ARRAY<INTERVAL>))])
=> "1"

SELECT COUNT(a) FROM (
  SELECT [INTERVAL 1 MONTH] AS a
  UNION ALL SELECT [INTERVAL 30 DAY]
  UNION ALL SELECT ARRAY<INTERVAL>[]
  UNION ALL SELECT ARRAY<INTERVAL>[NULL]
  UNION ALL SELECT CAST(NULL AS ARRAY<INTERVAL>)
)
=> "4"

SELECT COUNT(a) FROM (
  SELECT CAST(NULL AS ARRAY<INTERVAL>) AS a
)
=> "0"

SELECT COUNT(a) FROM (
  SELECT [i] AS a FROM UNNEST(ARRAY<INTERVAL>[]) AS i
)
=> "0"

SELECT ARRAY(
  SELECT COUNT(a) OVER (ORDER BY n ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
  FROM (
    SELECT 1 AS n, [INTERVAL 1 MONTH] AS a
    UNION ALL SELECT 2, CAST(NULL AS ARRAY<INTERVAL>)
    UNION ALL SELECT 3, ARRAY<INTERVAL>[]
    UNION ALL SELECT 4, ARRAY<INTERVAL>[NULL]
  ) ORDER BY n
)
=> [{"v":"1"},{"v":"1"},{"v":"1"},{"v":"2"}]
